title: Why this program
headline: No direct RCTs exist for pull-up progression schemes. This program is a synthesis from indirect evidence on frequency, volume, rest, proximity to failure, autoregulation, and eccentric training.

frequency.title: Frequency: 3×/week, ≥48h rest
frequency.body: Upper-body training benefits from ≥2 sessions/week. For latissimus and pulling muscles, 3×/week outperforms 1× when volume is matched. Recovery of strength within ~2 days supports a 48-hour minimum gap.

volume.title: Volume: 5 sets × 3 workouts = 15/week
volume.body: Dose-response meta-analyses show ≥10 hard sets per week beats ≤5 for strength. Our 15 weekly sets sit in the 12–20 optimal hypertrophy band without excessive fatigue.

workingSets.title: Working sets: submaximal ladder
workingSets.body: Four working sets at ~50–70% of anchor keep reps away from deep failure. Velocity-loss research on pull-ups supports stopping before excessive fatigue.

finalMax.title: Final set: Maximum (minimum N)
finalMax.body: One approach near failure provides progression signal and hypertrophy stimulus. The N submax + final AMRAP protocol as a whole was not tested in RCTs — extrapolation from proximity-to-failure literature.

rest.title: Rest: default 3 min
rest.body: 3–5 minutes between heavy sets preserves repetition output. Presets 90s (hypertrophy) and 5min (heavy) are configurable.

autoreg.title: Fail → repeat; 2 fails → deload
autoreg.body: Performance gating matches autoregulation literature. After two consecutive fails: M* := floor(0.9·M*), minimum 1.

retest.title: Retest every 2 cycles (~4 weeks)
retest.body: Formal max tests every two 6-step cycles recalibrate anchor. Also suggested after breaks >2 weeks.

path0.title: Path 0: negatives + assist
path0.body: Eccentric training has the strongest evidence for beginners who cannot pull concentrically. Scap pulls and hangs are coaching practice without direct RCTs — marked as extrapolation.

skips.title: Missed workouts: auto-shift
skips.body: Skipped steps stay next to perform. Later dates shift forward preserving intervals. Strength is maintained up to ~3 weeks — flexible scheduling supports habit formation.

items.name: Cycle end
items.formula: M*' = max(best final set in cycle, M* − 1)

sources.title: Sánchez-Moreno et al. 2020 — velocity loss in pull-ups
Ralston et al. 2018 — upper body frequency
Ralston et al. 2017 — weekly set volume
de Salles et al. 2009 — rest intervals
Roig et al. 2009 — eccentric training meta-analysis
